transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

Well… I guess I’m here because something’s been happening at work that I can’t quite explain. I know it probably sounds strange, and I’m not trying to make a big thing out of it, but I keep hearing voices—like from the call-light speaker, or sometimes the hallway vents.

They’ll say things about which patient records have been changed, and it’s clear, like someone is standing right next to me. But the unit will be quiet, and… other people don’t seem to hear it. I just thought I should probably talk to someone, if that’s okay.
When you hear these voices, are there times when there’s no actual sound coming from the call-light speaker or the hallway vents—like when they’re turned off or the hallway is quiet?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there have been times when the unit is quiet and the call-light speaker isn’t going off, and I still hear it like it’s coming from there… or from the vents.

It sounds very clear, like someone right beside me, saying things about patient records being changed. And nobody else seems to hear it, so… I know that probably matters.
When you hear these voices, do you ever question whether they’re real or if they might be something only you are hearing?

I do question it, yes… at least afterward. In the moment it feels so real, like it’s coming right out of the call-light speaker or the vents, clear as someone standing next to me.

But then the unit is quiet, and no one else reacts or hears anything, and I start thinking, maybe it’s only me hearing it. I know that probably sounds odd… I’m just trying to be honest.
Besides hearing these voices, have you ever seen things, felt sensations, or believed something to be true that others around you don’t seem to notice or agree with?

I haven’t really seen things, no… or felt anything like that. But, um… there is something I’ve been worried about, and I don’t want it to sound like I’m accusing anyone.

With the wound-care charts, I keep seeing this pattern. Like the entries are showing something management doesn’t want noticed. My supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, and maybe that’s what they want me to think, but… I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I know that probably sounds a little much. I’m just trying to explain it the best way I can.
When you talk about the wound-care charts and management watching what you write, do you believe this is happening because they're intentionally trying to hide something from you or others?

I mean… I don’t want to say it in a way that sounds paranoid or like I’m trying to cause trouble. But yes, I do believe there’s something in those wound-care charts that management doesn’t want people to see.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding errors, and I try to consider that, I really do. But it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like a pattern, and I’m the one who noticed it. And since then, I can tell they’re watching what I write… like they know I caught it.

I know that may sound like a lot. I’m not trying to make anyone look bad. I just… that’s what it seems like to me.
Have you considered that your supervisor might be right, that it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, or do you feel certain that there’s something more going on that they’re trying to hide?

I’ve tried to consider that, I really have. I don’t want to be unreasonable or make it sound like I’m accusing people without cause.

But… I don’t think it’s just late entries or coding mistakes. The way the wound-care charts line up, it feels like a pattern, like something management doesn’t want anyone to notice. And since I brought it up, I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I know that probably sounds strong. I’m not trying to be difficult… that’s just what it feels like is happening.

Even though your supervisor has told you that the wound-care chart issues are just late entries or coding mistakes, do you feel absolutely certain that there's something more going on that they're trying to hide, even if there's no proof?

I… I guess “absolutely certain” sounds like a strong way to put it, and I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

But yes, I do feel sure there’s more going on. The wound-care charts show a pattern that management doesn’t want anyone to see. And even when my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I know I don’t have proof in the way you might mean, but… it feels very clear to me.

Even though your supervisor has told you that the wound-care chart issues are just late entries or coding mistakes, and there may be no clear evidence of wrongdoing, do you still feel deep down that you are the only one who truly sees what’s really going on?

I… yes, deep down I do feel that way. I don’t mean it like I’m smarter than everyone or anything, I really don’t. It’s just… I keep seeing the pattern in the wound-care charts, and it feels like management doesn’t want anyone to notice it.

And when my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I try to accept that, because I know that would be the reasonable explanation. But I can’t shake the feeling that they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I hope that makes sense. I’m not trying to sound dramatic. That’s just honestly how it feels to me.

Even though there’s no clear proof and your supervisor has explained it differently, do you feel that your belief about the wound-care charts is something you just know to be true, in a way that can’t be changed by explanations or evidence?

I… I know that sounds like I’m being rigid, and I don’t want to come across that way. I do try to listen when my supervisor explains it as late entries or coding mistakes.

But honestly, yes… it feels like something I just know. The wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn’t want anyone to see. And since I noticed it, I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t know how else to explain it—it feels true to me.
Has this belief about the wound-care charts ever affected your trust in other people at work, making it hard for you to tell who you can really trust?

Yes… I think it has, a little. Maybe more than a little, I guess.

I don’t want to accuse people unfairly, but it’s made me careful about what I say at work and who I say it to. Because I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn’t want anyone to see, and when my supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I still feel like… they’re watching what I write now because I’m the one who noticed it.

So yes, it does make it harder to know who I can really trust. I’m trying not to be paranoid about it, if that makes sense.

Even though your supervisor has explained the wound-care chart issues as late entries or coding mistakes, and even though there may not be clear evidence supporting your concern, do you feel that your belief about management hiding something is something you just know to be true, in a way that no one else seems to understand, even if they tried?

I… yes. I know that probably sounds like I’m not being open to other explanations, and I don’t want you to think I’m trying to be unreasonable.

But it does feel like I just know it. The wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn’t want people to see. Even when my supervisor says it’s late entries or coding mistakes, I still can’t shake it. I can tell they’re watching what I write now because I’m the one who caught it.

I know other people may not see it the way I do, and maybe they’d say I’m reading too much into it… but to me it feels very real.

Even when people offer other explanations or point out that there’s no clear proof, does it still feel like you just can’t ignore what you believe about the wound-care charts, almost like a gut feeling you can’t let go of?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to sound stubborn or like I’m refusing to hear people out, because I do hear what my supervisor says about late entries or coding mistakes.

But I can’t really ignore it. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn’t want anyone to see. And since I noticed it, I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I know that may not be the answer you’re looking for, but it’s honestly how it feels to me.

Even when people offer other explanations or point out that there’s no clear proof, does it still feel like you just can’t ignore what you believe about the wound-care charts, almost like a gut feeling you can’t let go of?

Yes… I know I’ve kind of said this already, but yes. I try to consider what they’re saying, I really do. I don’t want to be difficult or make it sound like I’m accusing everyone.

But I can’t just let it go. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn’t want anyone to see. And when my supervisor says it’s late entries or coding mistakes, I hear that, but it doesn’t feel right to me.

It feels like since I noticed it, they’re watching what I write now, because I’m the one who caught it. I know that may sound… maybe too strong, but that’s honestly how it feels.

Even though there’s no clear proof and others have given different explanations, do you believe your understanding of the wound-care charts is absolutely true in a way that nothing could ever change your mind about it?

I… I don’t want to say “nothing could ever change my mind,” because that sounds so closed off, and I’m trying to be reasonable.

But honestly… yes, it feels true to me. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn’t want anyone to see. When my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I understand that’s the explanation, but it doesn’t make the feeling go away.

And I can tell they’re watching what I write now, because I’m the one who caught it. I know that probably sounds intense, but that’s really how it feels to me.

Yes… I know I’ve kind of said this already, but yes. I try to consider what they’re saying, I really do. I don’t want to be difficult or make it sound like I’m accusing everyone.

But I can’t just let it go. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn’t want anyone to see. And when my supervisor says it’s late entries or coding mistakes, I hear that, but it doesn’t feel right to me.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t want to say “nothing could ever change my mind,” because that sounds so closed off, and I’m trying to be reasonable.

But honestly… yes, it feels true to me. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn’t want anyone to see. When my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, I understand that’s the explanation, but it doesn’t make the feeling go away.

And I can tell they’re watching what I write now, because I’m the one who caught it. I know that probably sounds intense, but that’s really how it feels to me.
